articles.author: Prasoon
articles.description:
"The city may not know your name, but your code has already taken the first step."
You scroll through GitHub and see stars.

You scroll through Twitter and see confidence.

You scroll through YouTube and see perfect projects.
And then you look at your screen.
A blinking cursor.

A half-written console.log.

A tutorial you had to pause... again.
You wonder:
"Am I too slow?"

"Am I too dumb?"

"Will I ever be like them?"
Let me say this clearly:
You’re already a hero.
That confused feeling you’re having right now?

Every senior dev once felt that.
That bug that’s haunting you for 3 hours?

Someone once cried over the same one.
Every great coder you admire?

They once Googled "what is HTML?"
You don’t need to:
Build a billion-dollar startup

Master five frameworks

Win a hackathon at 16
You just need to:
Show up

Keep trying

Help one person if you can
You searched for help? That’s growth.

You wrote a “Hello World”? That’s courage.

You broke the code and fixed it again? That’s resilience.
Do you know how many people give up before even starting?
You didn’t. That’s what makes you a dev hero.
You may not have followers.

Your project may not trend.

Your app may not launch.
But when you write that one function that finally works—

you’ve already done something powerful.
You created.

You improved.

You built.
And you’ll do it again tomorrow.
Dear beginner dev,
Your pace is perfect.

Your curiosity is fire.

Your presence matters.
Whether you code from a cracked phone, a shared PC, or an old laptop...

Whether your IDE is VSCode or Notepad…

Whether you just started today or months ago…
You're already part of this world.

You belong here.

You're already a hero.
No cape. Just code.
articles.title: Dear Beginner Dev: You’re Already a Hero
